title: Sunset Session

conditions.headline: Chip Wipeout: Nasdaq Gets Tumbled as Nvidia Drama Churns the Lineup
conditions.summary: Stocks fell hard on Monday as Nvidia's leadership turmoil, new chip export limits and higher yields sank tech. The Nasdaq lost about 2.5 percent and the S&P 500 nearly 2 percent ahead of Nvidia's earnings tomorrow.

sections.title: Closing Bell
items: The S&P 500 fell 1.92% to 7,416.59, the Nasdaq Composite dropped 2.49% to 24,509.76, and the Dow lost 1.41% to 51,608.17.
The Russell 2000 slid 1.70% to 2,742.94.
Nvidia's leadership crisis drove the selloff; shares hit session lows after a report that the board is not considering bringing back Jensen Huang.
A new Commerce Department rule on remote access to advanced chips and rising Treasury yields added pressure on tech.
Selling started at the open and deepened in the last two hours, with the Nasdaq taking its steepest losses late.
Semiconductors and megacap tech led the decline; real estate held up best, and health insurers were among the few gainers.
The VIX jumped nearly 20% to about 23.

sections.title: Macro & Fed
items: The Empire State manufacturing index fell to 7.8 for November, well below the roughly 16.7 expected and down about 18 points from October.
Fed Governor Michelle Bowman sounded hawkish on corporate debt levels and the risks if the AI boom disappoints.
Fed Chair Kevin Warsh spoke at a midday conference as investors watched for policy signals.
The 10-year Treasury yield hovered near 5.15%, a level weighing on growth stocks.
Oil fell, with WTI down about 3.7% to near $85, as Strait of Hormuz shipments recovered despite weekend tensions with Iran.

sections.title: Biggest Movers
items: TSN (Tyson Foods): +8.7% — earnings topped hopes and its beef outlook cheered investors.
ELV (Elevance Health): +3.8% — health insurers caught a bid on a down day.
HUM (Humana): +2.7% — joined the health insurer rally.
INTC (Intel): -7.0% — hit by a shareholder class action lawsuit.
DELL (Dell Technologies): -7.0% — sold off amid warnings about industry debt.
AMD (Advanced Micro Devices): -5.6% — pressured by new chip export restrictions.
NVDA (Nvidia): -4.1% — board reportedly not considering a return for Jensen Huang, a day before earnings.
GOOGL (Alphabet): -3.8% — megacap tech sold off broadly.

sections.title: Earnings Today & Tonight
items: Tyson Foods jumped about 8.7% after its fiscal fourth-quarter report, even as it guided to lower sales next year.
iQIYI sank about 17% after posting third-quarter results before the open.
XPeng rose early after third-quarter revenue grew about 19% and it guided for 169,000 to 174,000 deliveries in the fourth quarter.
Ballard Power fell about 8% after third-quarter revenue dropped 31%.
After the bell, C3.ai slipped about 7% in extended trading.

sections.title: Business News
items: Anthropic's IPO is expected to price Wednesday night and start trading Thursday, at a target valuation around $1.4 trillion.
Bank of America's CEO said the Anthropic deal is pushing some smaller listings into 2027.
The Commerce Department issued a rule targeting remote access to advanced chips by offshore data centers serving Chinese firms.
Telus jumped on an unsolicited, non-binding proposal from Quebecor.
Novo Nordisk rose after Phase 3 CagriSema data showed about 21% weight loss at 68 weeks.

sections.title: On Deck
items: 7:30 AM CT: October retail sales (forecasts range from flat to +0.2%) and import prices.
8:15 AM CT: October industrial production; 9:00 AM CT: business inventories and the NAHB housing index.
Before the open: Home Depot and Disney report earnings.
After the close: Nvidia reports, with options pricing in about an 8% move.
Fed speakers: Musalem, Waller, Hammack and Williams.

Give the crew a good evening woof, Gus! Alright, let's paddle through it. The Final Set. The S and P five hundred fell one point nine percent to seven thousand four hundred sixteen. The Nasdaq got tumbled, down two and a half percent to twenty four thousand five hundred ten. The Dow lost one point four percent to fifty one thousand six hundred eight. The Russell two thousand slid one point seven percent. The big swell came from Nvidia. A report said the board is not considering bringing back Jensen Huang, and the stock dropped to its lows of the day. A new Commerce Department rule on chip exports and higher bond yields made the water even choppier. Selling got gnarly in the last two hours. Chip stocks and big tech led the wipeout, while real estate held up best. The fear gauge, the VIX, jumped nearly twenty percent. Wind and Weather. The Empire State factory index dropped to seven point eight, way below the roughly sixteen point seven that was expected. Fed Governor Michelle Bowman sounded a warning on corporate debt and the risks if the A I boom falls short. The ten year Treasury yield sat near five point one five percent. Crude oil fell almost four percent to around eighty five dollars, and gold slipped about one percent. Now The Lineup. Tyson Foods rode a clean wave all the way to the beach, up almost nine percent after its earnings beat. Gus, that's worth a biscuit! Here you go, buddy! Health insurers Elevance and Humana also found some glassy water. On the wipeout side, Intel fell seven percent on a shareholder lawsuit. Dell dropped seven percent. A M D lost more than five percent on the export rules, and Nvidia fell four percent. Alphabet slid almost four percent. The Tide Chart. Besides Tyson, i Q I Y I sank about seventeen percent after its results. Ballard Power fell after revenue dropped thirty one percent. After the bell, C three dot A I slipped about seven percent. Beach Talk. The Anthropic I P O is set to price Wednesday night and trade Thursday, at a target near one point four trillion dollars. That's no grommet, that's a whole new Kahuna paddling out. Telus jumped on a takeover proposal from Quebecor, and Novo Nordisk rose on strong weight loss drug data. Tomorrow's Forecast. Retail sales hit at seven thirty A M Central, with industrial production at eight fifteen. Home Depot and Disney report before the open. The big one is Nvidia after the close, with options pricing in about an eight percent move. Fed speakers include Waller and Williams. So wax that board and get some rest.
